extracted.intended_audience: scientists and academic readers of Nature (physicists, chemists) and scientific job applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and expectations for reviewing or assessing scientific books (here: a book on the electron theory) and related institutional hiring/application requirements appearing on the same journal page. Covers both evaluative dimensions of a scientific monograph and procedural standards for academic appointments advertised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author reputation / authority
rubrics_metrics.description: A book on a difficult subject by an illuminating and inspiring publicist such as Sir Oliver Lodge is 'doubly acceptable'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review emphasizes that the author's stature and publicist skill increases the book's acceptability and value to readers when the topic is obscure or 'mystified'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and capacity to illuminate a mystified topic
rubrics_metrics.description: The book should be 'illuminating and inspiring' and make a 'complete mystification' accessible to readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularly for subjects where 'a more complete mystification exists', clarity and exposition that reveal the subject's structure and meaning are highly valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with recent research and experimental findings
rubrics_metrics.description: The work should address recent important results (e.g., J. J. Thomson's investigations and measured constants) and integrate their implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers expect discussion of the latest influential experiments and papers and how they alter or challenge existing theories—failure to do so weakens a scientific book's relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of difficulties and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The author should not attempt to minimise recent difficulties; the electromagnetic theory 'must be regarded for the present as no better than a working hypothesis'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly stating the epistemic status of the theory (hypothesis vs. proof) is important; the reviewer highlights and approves a frank statement of limits and uncertainties in the preface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced tone: enthusiastic yet critical
rubrics_metrics.description: The author may retain enthusiasm for a theory's ultimate prospects while being aware of and not minimising the magnitude of recent difficulties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good scientific treatment combines informed optimism with critical awareness rather than unqualified advocacy or dismissive scepticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based argumentation and connection to theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments and claims should be connected to experimental measurements and theoretical work (for example, measurements of electron constants and J. J. Thomson's models).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer values treatments that ground speculative extensions of theory in the empirical and theoretical literature that produced them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit statement of epistemic status (prefatory honesty)
rubrics_metrics.description: The preface should clearly state whether a proposed theory has 'proof' or is a 'working hypothesis', acknowledging that its truth may remain 'an open question'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefatory clarity about what is established versus speculative guides readers' expectations and is treated positively by the reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of appendices, notes, and references to recent authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The inclusion of appended notes and references to recent authorities and updates is a positive structural feature ('some notes have been added', 'An appendix refers to recent authorities').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing appendices and up-to-date references helps place historical material in current context and aids scholarly usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautious treatment of speculative or local conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions of local or speculative nature (e.g., claimed connections between thunderstorms and sun-spot frequency) 'must be regarded with some reserve.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bold or speculative claims should be presented cautiously and flagged as tentative when evidence is limited or of local scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: University degree required for teaching appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: Many advertised posts state 'University degree, or its equivalent, essential.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possession of a university degree (or equivalent) is a strict eligibility requirement for numerous academic and teaching positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant teaching or institutional experience required
rubrics_metrics.description: For some posts (e.g., 'FIRST ASSISTANT in the Physics Department') 'experience in a University College or Technical Institute essential'; others require 'teaching experience absolutely essential.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior experience in comparable educational institutions or demonstrable teaching experience is a substantive selection criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of testimonials / supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be accompanied by 'copies of testimonials' or similar supporting documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates are required to enclose testimonials or references with their application forms for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specified application forms and prescribed submission procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of forms and particulars 'may be obtained by sending a stamped, addressed, foolscap envelope' and forms must be used for applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow the advertised procedural steps to obtain and submit the correct application materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict application deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Each appointment lists a hard deadline: 'The last day for receiving applications is Wednesday, May 30' (and similar dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting the stated deadline is mandatory; late applications will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for specific practical skills or knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Some posts give preference for candidates 'having a good knowledge of Field Work' (e.g., Horticultural College).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical or domain-specific skills (fieldwork, laboratory technique) can be preferred or desirable selection factors beyond formal qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency / post-specific conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain posts carry conditions such as being 'Resident' and specify initial salary terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be willing and able to meet role-specific conditions like residency and accept stated terms of employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender-restricted appointments (as advertised)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some advertisements specify 'Applications from Women only' for particular posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adverts may restrict eligibility by gender (reflecting historical hiring practices); applicants must note and comply with any such restrictions stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of teaching staff for correspondence tuition
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence tuition staff 'includes graduates of Oxford, Cambridge, London, and Royal Universities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions advertise staff credentials as an implicit quality criterion for their tuition services; prospective students assess suitability based on tutor qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality guarantee / refund policy for specimen collections
rubrics_metrics.description: If the collection is unsatisfactory, return at the company's expense within ten days and they will immediately refund money in full; they take risk of loss or breakage and cost of double transport.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This refund/quality guarantee is presented as an assurance of product quality and customer satisfaction—failure to meet expectations triggers a full refund within the specified period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument conformity to standards / certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain instruments are offered with the note that 'All the above Instruments will pass the Kew Observatory test' and Kew Certificates can be provided for an extra fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing established observatory/instrumentation tests and providing certificates is used as a quality standard for scientific apparatus.
